newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall with U.S., rate concerns rise.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall with U.S., rate concerns rise.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower late Thursday as a sharp drop in U.S. bonds dragged the market lower.
"The market is watching the long bond yield tick by tick," said a trader at a local bank. The U.S. 30-year bond yield was last at 6.96 percent, up eight basis points.
The release of strong U.S. February retail sales figures and an upward revision in January's figure sparked the U.S. market slide as concerns of a U.S. rate hike rose.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 shed $0.35 to 126.00.
But the market was still taking comfort in the possibility of an upgrade by Standard & Poor's in Argentina's debt rating, leading it to outperform other markets in the region.
"Argentina has been doing better than the other markets. Evidently, the S&P news is helping," said an analyst at a foreign bank.

However, even if the outlook on Argentina's debt was changed to 'positive' from 'stable' or there was an outright upgrade to its BB- rating, the analyst did not think the market would rise if the U.S. markets continue to fall. "It will just fall less than other markets," the analyst said.

Fears increased Thursday over U.S. rates after the retail sales data and comments by Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Michael Moskow where he talked of a preemptive policy to foil inflationary pressures by the Federal Reserve.
With U.S. producer prices due out on Friday and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting scheduled for March 25, the U.S. market could well slide further, pressuring Argentine bonds.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 6.13 percent.
